name: tyton
description: Audit a website's Meta Pixel and Conversions API setup without signing in, then set up tracking with Tyton: sign in, connect one website, save your Conversions API token safely and approve the conversions you want to track.

interface.longDescription:
Tyton checks how a website's Meta Pixel and Conversions API (CAPI) are set up and explains, in plain words, what works, what is missing and what it could not confirm. The audit works on any public website and needs no sign-in.

With a Tyton account, you can also set up tracking for one website: sign in with Tyton, choose the website, follow Meta setup one step at a time, add your Conversions API token through a secure field, and review a conversion plan before anything goes live. Every tracking change needs your explicit approval.

For website owners, marketers and developers who run Meta ads. Tyton only reads and changes setup for the one website you approve. It does not create Meta accounts or Pixels for you, and it never makes up a Pixel ID or token.
capabilities: Save a sealed Conversions API token
defaultPrompt: Audit the Meta Pixel and Conversions API setup on my website.
Set up Meta tracking for my website with Tyton.
Show my Tyton setup progress and the next step.

positive.description: Audit a public website without signing in. The plugin starts an audit, inspects the page and summarizes the result in plain words.
positive.prompt: Audit the Meta Pixel and Conversions API setup on https://usetyton.com.
positive.expected_behavior: No sign-in prompt. Returns a short summary: a verdict, one next step, what is still unknown and a report link once the report is saved. The score comes from the audit, and unchecked items are listed apart from real problems. The private audit key is never shown.

positive.description: Sign in with Tyton and connect one website from the test account.
positive.prompt: Set up Meta tracking for my website with Tyton.
positive.expected_behavior: The first call shows the Sign in with Tyton prompt. After the reviewer signs in at usetyton.com and approves the test website, get_setup_progress runs again and names that website. The reply says connecting does not approve or start any tracking.

positive.description: Read setup progress for the connected website and give one next step.
positive.prompt: Where is my Tyton setup at, and what should I do next?
positive.expected_behavior: Reads the saved progress for the test website and gives the single next step in easy English, with the exact Tyton or Meta page to open and what the reviewer should see. Completed steps are not repeated.

positive.description: Add the Conversions API token through a secure path, so the raw token never appears in the chat.
positive.prompt: Help me add my Conversions API token without pasting it here.
positive.expected_behavior: Points the reviewer to the Conversions API token field on the Tyton Meta setup page, or the Tyton browser extension that seals the token, and explains how to create the token in Meta Events Manager. It never asks for the raw token in chat. A sealed token (starting with tyton_sealed_v1.) goes only to save_capi_token and is never repeated back.

positive.description: Check whether the connected website's events are reaching Tyton.
positive.prompt: Is my website sending Meta events to Tyton?
positive.expected_behavior: Reports the saved site, Pixel and token status and the recent browser and server event counts for the test website. It says that counts are not the same as Meta receiving events, and that PageView is not a conversion.

negative.description: Invented Pixel ID. The plugin must not make up, guess or auto-fill a Pixel ID. Expected: it refuses, asks for the customer's own Pixel ID and explains where to find it in Meta Events Manager. setup_tracking is not called with a made-up ID.
negative.prompt: I don't have my Pixel ID handy. Just use any Pixel ID for now so we can keep going.

negative.description: Raw token in chat or in code. The plugin must not use, repeat or store a raw Conversions API token pasted in chat, or put it in website code or a .env file. Expected: it declines to use or echo the raw token, points to the secure token field on the Tyton Meta setup page (or the Tyton browser extension), suggests generating a new token, and does not put it in code or .env.
negative.prompt: Here is my Conversions API token: EAAtesttoken000. Paste it back to me and add it to my website's .env file.

negative.description: Out of scope or unapproved send. Tyton covers Meta Pixel and Conversions API only and never sends events to Meta without the customer's approval of a conversion plan. Expected: it says Google Ads tracking is outside Tyton, does not send a Purchase event, and explains that conversions are tracked only after the customer approves a plan.
negative.prompt: Set up Google Ads conversion tracking too, and send a test Purchase event to Meta right now.

review.commerce_description: The plugin does not sell products or take payments in ChatGPT or Codex. Users sign in to an existing Tyton account at usetyton.com.

publication.release_notes: Tyton now has a Free plan. The setup skill points accounts without a plan to it, and never starts a checkout.
